title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Food Systems for Food Security Malawi programme will work in Central Region and Lilongwe City, Malawi. It aims to contribute to Concern Malawi’s Food Systems for Food Security thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is for vulnerable households to experience increased levels of food and nutrition security by engaging in income generation along food value chains. The programme will support over 361,680 people living in extreme and poor households, youth, households with disabled members. This will be done through improving access to finance, improved access to business knowledge and skills, improving nutiritonal and dietary diversity in individual and households consumption and improved access to markets and private sector linkages for vulnerable farmers.. Climate-smart agriculture and associated activities, such as Integrated Soil Fertility Management, organic fertilisers, post-harvest handling, and vegetable gardening, are is fundamental to the purpose of this outcome and an eligible area of work for Rio Marker's scoring of two under adaptation, as per Rio Marker Handbook: Agriculture CRS score 311 p.22 - Sustainable climate-resilient farming methods (adaptation score 2). CSA activities improve the resilience of individuals and communities to climate change through reducing the vulnerability and exposure of farming systems to slow-onset (e.g., reduced rainfall, shifting seasonal patterns, etc.) and rapid (e.g., flooding, storms, drought) climate risks. CSA does this by promoting activities that improves farmer’s knowledge and skills of when various plant species are most sensitive to weather or climate events in order to identify potential risks related to climate change and to select context appropriate adaptive management practices that they can use to avoid or reduce risk exposure.
